title: CDICF Component Manifest
description: Canonical knowledge unit for one component, primitive, block, page, composition, hook, theme, adapter or effect in the CDICF. A collection of code becomes intelligence-selectable infrastructure only once every member carries one of these. Enum values in provenance.license_tier and provenance.redistribution_posture are the vocabulary of lib/license_gate.js and must not diverge from it -- validate_manifest.js imports the gate and fails if they do.

id.description: Stable key, '<namespace>/<component>'. Never reused after retirement.

version.description: Upstream version, or 'unversioned' when the upstream ships none.

commit_sha.description: 40-hex pin, or PENDING_CLONE. Never a branch name -- a branch is not a pin.

copyright_holder.description: Exactly as the license text states it. An empty holder is never valid -- an MIT notice cannot be written without a name. minLength alone was insufficient: whitespace has length, so '   ' satisfied it and produced exactly the nameless notice this field exists to prevent (A5-LEG-04). The pattern requires one non-whitespace character.

motion_budget.description: Cost this component draws from the project's DESIGN.md motion budget.

known_failures.description: Empty array means none recorded -- NOT that none exist. Absence of evidence is recorded as unassessed elsewhere, never as a pass.

retirement_condition.description: What would end this component's life. A capability admitted with no retirement condition can never be removed on evidence, only on opinion.

identity_fit_score.description: How well this survives the DESIGN_GOVERNANCE logo-swap test. Low means generic.

abstention_conditions.description: Contexts in which the selector must decline to use this component. Abstention is a valid outcome.

alternatives.description: Manifest ids of substitutes, for the substitution graph.

cdicfInvariants.rule: provenance.redistribution_posture MUST equal the posture lib/license_gate.js derives from provenance.license_tier.
cdicfInvariants.why: The two vocabularies are one vocabulary. A manifest that says PERMISSIVE/prohibited or SOURCE_AVAILABLE_RESTRICTED/allowed is internally inconsistent and would be trusted by an installer.

This is the structural form of the react-bits decision. A prohibited component recorded as fork_canonical is a license violation waiting for an emitter to act on it. Enforced here so the rule survives everyone forgetting it.
Provenance may never be stripped from restricted code.

cdicfInvariants.rule: confidence 'VERIFIED' REQUIRES commit_sha and license_fingerprint to both be pinned (neither PENDING_CLONE).
cdicfInvariants.why: VERIFIED is a claim about a specific artifact. Unpinned, there is no artifact the claim is about.
Recommending a component whose accessibility was never measured launders an unknown into a recommendation.
High motion without a reduced-motion path is an accessibility failure, not a style choice.
